themeDescription: Understanding living things and the human body

days.title: Why Jungles Are So Alive
days.learning_objective: Caves form through erosion and can contain unique ecosystems.
learning_objectives: Describe the process of cave formation through erosion.
Identify at least three unique adaptations of cave-dwelling organisms.
Explain the importance of cave conservation and responsible exploration.

days.title: The Power of Grass
days.learning_objective: Insects are the most diverse group of animals on Earth.
learning_objectives: Identify at least five different orders of insects.
Describe the basic life cycle of a butterfly and a grasshopper.
Explain at least three ways insects are important to the environment.

days.title: Why Wetlands Matter
days.learning_objective: Birds are the only animals with feathers and most can fly.
learning_objectives: Identify the key characteristics that define a bird.
Explain the purpose and function of feathers.
Describe how bird anatomy contributes to their ability to fly.

days.title: Cities Under the Sea
days.learning_objective: Fish breathe underwater using gills and come in countless varieties.
learning_objectives: Identify that fish breathe underwater using gills.
Name at least three different types of fish and describe their habitats.
Explain the importance of fish in the food chain and marine ecosystems.

days.title: Worlds Without Light
days.learning_objective: Mammals feed their young with milk and have hair or fur.
learning_objectives: Identify two defining characteristics of mammals (hair/fur and milk production).
Name at least five different mammals and describe their habitats.
Explain the importance of mammals in the ecosystem.

days.title: How Islands Are Born
days.learning_objective: Reptiles are cold-blooded and most lay eggs on land.
learning_objectives: Identify at least three key characteristics of reptiles.
Explain the difference between cold-blooded and warm-blooded animals.
Describe the reptile life cycle, including egg-laying or live birth.
Recognize at least five different types of reptiles and their habitats.

days.title: What's Living in the Dirt
days.learning_objective: Amphibians live both in water and on land during their lives.
learning_objectives: Identify the three main types of amphibians: frogs, salamanders, and caecilians.
Explain the amphibian life cycle, including metamorphosis.
Describe at least three adaptations that allow amphibians to live in both water and on land.

days.title: The Stories Rocks Tell
days.learning_objective: Plants create their own food using sunlight through photosynthesis.
learning_objectives: Identify the basic needs of plants for survival.
Explain the process of photosynthesis in simple terms.
Describe the importance of plants for oxygen production and food supply.

days.title: Earth's Hidden Treasures
days.learning_objective: Trees are the largest and longest-living plants on Earth.
learning_objectives: Identify at least three different parts of a tree and their functions.
Explain the importance of trees for the environment and human life.
Describe the process of photosynthesis in simple terms.

days.title: How Gems Are Made
days.learning_objective: Flowers attract pollinators and produce seeds for new plants.
learning_objectives: Identify the main parts of a flower and their functions.
Explain the process of pollination and its importance.
Describe how flowers produce seeds and create new plants.

days.title: Where Metals Come From
days.learning_objective: Mushrooms are fungi that help decompose organic matter.
learning_objectives: Define fungi and identify mushrooms as a type of fungi.
Explain the role of mushrooms in decomposition of organic matter.
Describe the importance of decomposition for soil health and plant growth.

days.title: What's In the Air You Breathe
days.learning_objective: Bacteria are microscopic organisms found everywhere on Earth.
learning_objectives: Define bacteria and describe their basic structure.
Identify the diverse environments where bacteria can be found.
Explain the beneficial and harmful roles of bacteria in everyday life.

days.title: Why We Need Oxygen
days.learning_objective: The human body contains trillions of cells working together.
learning_objectives: Identify the basic components of the human body (cells, tissues, organs, systems).
Explain that the human body contains trillions of cells.
Describe the general function of a few major organ systems (e.g., circulatory, respiratory, digestive).

days.title: Carbon Is Everywhere
days.learning_objective: The brain controls our thoughts, movements, and memories.
learning_objectives: Identify the main parts of the brain and their functions.
Explain how neurons communicate with each other.
Describe how memories are formed and stored in the brain.

days.title: The Gas You Don't Notice
days.learning_objective: The heart pumps blood throughout the body every moment of life.
learning_objectives: Identify the major parts of the heart (atria, ventricles, valves).
Explain how the heart pumps blood throughout the body.
Describe the importance of heart health and ways to maintain it.

days.title: The Simplest Element
days.learning_objective: Bones provide structure and protect our vital organs.
learning_objectives: Identify the main functions of the skeletal system.
Describe the basic structure of a bone.
Explain how bones protect vital organs.
List several healthy habits that support bone health.

days.title: Building Blocks of Everything
days.learning_objective: Muscles contract and relax to create all body movements.
learning_objectives: Identify the three main types of muscles: skeletal, smooth, and cardiac.
Explain how muscles contract and relax to produce movement.
Describe the importance of exercise and nutrition for healthy muscles.

days.title: When Atoms Connect
days.learning_objective: Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell in the body.
learning_objectives: Identify the four main components of blood: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma.
Explain the primary function of blood in transporting oxygen and nutrients to cells and removing waste products.
Describe the roles of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets in maintaining health and fighting infection.

days.title: The Tiny Units of Life
days.learning_objective: Skin is our largest organ and protects us from the environment.
learning_objectives: Identify the main layers of the skin (epidermis, dermis, hypodermis).
Explain the protective functions of the skin against germs and UV radiation.
Describe how skin helps regulate body temperature through sweat glands.
List three ways to care for and protect their skin.

days.title: Your Body's Instruction Manual
days.learning_objective: Eyes detect light and allow us to see the world in color.
learning_objectives: Identify the main parts of the eye and their functions.
Explain how light enables us to see objects and colors.
Describe common vision problems and how they are corrected.

days.title: What Blood Does All Day
days.learning_objective: Ears detect sound waves and help us maintain balance.
learning_objectives: Identify the main parts of the ear and their functions.
Explain how sound waves travel through the ear to the brain.
Describe how the ear helps maintain balance.
Identify ways to protect their hearing from damage.

days.title: How Taste Works
days.learning_objective: Taste helps us identify safe and nutritious foods.
learning_objectives: Identify the five basic tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami.
Explain the role of taste in identifying safe and nutritious foods.
Describe the connection between taste and smell.
Conduct a simple taste test and record observations.

days.title: Why Smell Triggers Memory
days.learning_objective: Smell is closely linked to memory and emotion.
learning_objectives: Identify the main parts of the olfactory system and their functions.
Explain the connection between smell, memory, and emotion.
Apply knowledge of scent to create a 'memory jar' reflecting personal experiences.

days.title: How Skin Feels Things
days.learning_objective: Touch allows us to feel texture, temperature, and pain.
learning_objectives: Identify the different types of sensations our skin can detect.
Explain how nerve endings in the skin transmit information to the brain.
Describe the importance of touch for safety and interaction with the environment.

days.title: How Your Eyes See
days.learning_objective: Emotions are complex responses that guide our behavior.
learning_objectives: Identify and name a variety of emotions.
Explain the purpose and function of emotions.
Apply strategies for managing and regulating emotions in healthy ways.

days.title: How Your Ears Work
days.learning_objective: Happiness comes from connections, purpose, and gratitude.
learning_objectives: Define happiness and identify its key components: connections, purpose, and gratitude.
Identify and practice at least three strategies for cultivating gratitude in daily life.
Develop a personal action plan to foster stronger connections and find greater purpose.

days.title: Your Heart Never Stops
days.learning_objective: Sadness is a natural response to loss and disappointment.
learning_objectives: Identify sadness as a natural human emotion.
Describe personal experiences that trigger feelings of sadness.
Develop healthy coping strategies for managing sadness.

days.title: What Your Brain Does
days.learning_objective: Fear protects us by alerting us to potential dangers.
learning_objectives: Define fear and identify its common triggers.
Explain the physiological response to fear (fight, flight, freeze).
Describe the evolutionary purpose of fear for survival.
Develop strategies for managing and coping with fear in healthy ways.

days.title: How Lungs Breathe for You
days.learning_objective: Anger signals that something feels unfair or threatening.
learning_objectives: Identify the common triggers and physical symptoms of anger.
Explain the difference between healthy and unhealthy expressions of anger.
Practice at least three different anger management techniques, such as deep breathing or progressive muscle relaxation.

days.title: Your Body's Framework
days.learning_objective: Surprise occurs when something unexpected happens.
learning_objectives: Define 'surprise' and identify its key components.
Explain how surprise affects the brain and learning process.
Recognize the role of surprise in creativity and innovation.

days.title: What Love Does to Us
days.learning_objective: Love creates deep bonds between people and living things.
learning_objectives: Define different types of love and affection.
Identify ways to express love and kindness towards others.
Explain how love fosters stronger relationships between people and living things.
